sections.skill: Decide what must be true, what could be true and what cannot be true in a constrained arrangement

questions.prompt: A club holds five talks, Fossils, Gears, Honey, Jazz and Kites, one on each day from Monday to Friday. Conditions: (1) Gears is earlier in the week than Jazz. (2) Honey is on Wednesday or Friday. (3) Fossils and Kites are not on consecutive days. (4) Jazz is not on Friday. Which statement MUST be true?

choices.text: Gears is on Monday or Tuesday.

questions.correct_answer: Gears is on Monday or Tuesday.

(3) Fossils and Kites are not on consecutive days. (4) Jazz is not on Friday. How many complete schedules meet all four conditions?

(3) Fossils and Kites are not on consecutive days. (4) Jazz is not on Friday. Suppose Honey is on Wednesday. Using Monday = 1, Tuesday = 2, Wednesday = 3, Thursday = 4 and Friday = 5, give a day number Kites could be on.
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: k == 1 or k == 2 or k == 5 (example: k = 5)

sections.skill: Strategy: list every case, then read must, could, cannot
sections.relationship: Students guess from one schedule. Listing every schedule that meets the conditions turns each question into a check: true in all, true in some, or true in none.
sections.author_note: Students guess from one schedule. Listing every schedule that meets the conditions turns each question into a check: true in all, true in some, or true in none.

lesson.title: List every case, then read must, could and cannot
text: Find every arrangement that meets all the conditions. Organize the list by one item with few choices, so no case is missed.
A statement MUST be true if it is true in every arrangement on the list.
It COULD be true if it is true in at least one. It CANNOT be true if it is true in none.

example.title: Worked example (a different puzzle)
prompt: Three chores, dishes (D), laundry (L) and sweeping (W), are done on days 1, 2, 3, one per day. Conditions: laundry is not on day 3; dishes are after sweeping.
steps: Laundry on day 1: W, D fill days 2 and 3 with W first: L, W, D.
Laundry on day 2: W on day 1, D on day 3: W, L, D.
Dishes are on day 3 in both, so "dishes are on day 3" must be true. "Laundry is on day 1" could be true. "Sweeping is on day 3" cannot be true.

questions.prompt: Three talks, P, Q and R, are on days 1, 2 and 3, one per day. Conditions: P is not on day 1; Q is earlier than R. How many schedules meet both conditions?
Three talks, P, Q and R, are on days 1, 2 and 3, one per day. Conditions: P is not on day 1; Q is earlier than R. Then Q must be on day 1.
Three talks, P, Q and R, are on days 1, 2 and 3, one per day. Conditions: P is not on day 1; Q is earlier than R. Then R must be on day 3.
In a scheduling puzzle, what does it mean to say a statement CANNOT be true?

choices.text: It is not mentioned in any of the conditions.
It is false in every schedule that meets the conditions.
It is false in at least one schedule that meets the conditions.
It is true in exactly one schedule that meets the conditions.

questions.correct_answer: It is false in every schedule that meets the conditions.
